cards.title: Top of the Ladder
cards.instruction: Carry yourself as the highest-status person present. Treat questions as requests for your approval.

cards.title: Help Me Keep This Quiet
cards.instruction: Get someone to help contain a secret without first revealing its full risk or purpose.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll decide how we handle this. Hide this envelope under the picnic hamper before Mum comes in.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: She asked me to unpack the hamper.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You can question the details after my decision. Then keep the envelope in your pocket while you unpack.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'll end up taking it home.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Perfect. I'll explain when she stops asking where it is.

cardFidelity.evidence: A1 assigns hiding, A3 postpones scrutiny and orders pocket storage, and A5 approves removal while keeping the reason withheld.

responseLogic.evidence: B2 unpacking threatens the hiding place; A3 moves it to a pocket; B4 leaving with it becomes A5 desired outcome.

relationship.evidence: B2 and B4 are practical consequences of the task, with B not yet knowing the secret's purpose.

heightening.evidence: A5 converts accidental removal into extended containment and further delayed disclosure.

specificity.evidence: A1 Mum, envelope and hamper establish a concrete concealment task.

brevityWit.evidence: A5 explain when she stops asking is an earned disclosure delay, not a new unprepared secret.
